stories.headline: Targets Fall Across AI Chips: Stifel Cuts Marvell to $280 as Barron's Calls Memory Stocks 'Agonizingly Cheap'
stories.summary: Stifel cut its Marvell target to $280 from $370 on 20 Nov while keeping a Buy rating, using a lower 21.5 times 2028 earnings multiple and warning that slower data-centre capex in 2028-29 could delay product ramps. Needham trimmed its target to $300 from $400 and TD Cowen downgraded to Hold, citing possible dilution from Marvell's all-stock purchase of Lumentum, valued at about $115bn, which lifts its share count by about 49%. Marvell fell 22% in the week to 20 Nov. Barron's argued on 20 Nov that memory makers are 'agonizingly cheap', with Micron at 3.8 times next year's expected earnings, SK Hynix at 3.1 and Samsung at 2.5, even as Micron dropped about 13% that day to around $603, about half its June record.
stories.market: MRVL reports on 1 Dec; MU, WDC (-12%), SNDK (-15%) and STX (-12%) were all sharply lower by midday on 20 Nov, so valuation arguments are colliding with momentum selling.

body: Marvell has become a test case for how brokers handle the AI-chip rout. Stifel's cut to $280 from $370 rests on lower comparable valuations, while Needham's move to $300 from $400 and TD Cowen's downgrade to Hold focus on the dilution and timing of the Lumentum deal, under which each Lumentum share converts into 4.5 Marvell shares. Oppenheimer reiterated Buy with a $425 target, and William Blair kept Outperform while flagging integration risk.

Marvell's share price was about $138.47 in the Investing.com report, far below its 52-week high of $329.88. The company has guided to October-quarter revenue of about $3.15bn, roughly 52% higher than a year earlier.

In the memory group, Barron's writer Jack Denton argued on 20 Nov that valuations are extremely low: Micron at 3.8 times expected next-year earnings, compared with 15-20 times for many S&P 500 stocks, and an average analyst target implying almost 150% upside. He cautioned that bad news could make the stocks cheaper still.
The article ran on a day when Micron fell about 13% to roughly $603 by midday, about 50% below its 25 June record close of $1,213.56.

stories.headline: Argentina's Country Risk Ends the Week Near 1,070 as Analysts Flag a $7.75 Billion 2027 Funding Hole
stories.summary: Argentina's country-risk spread closed Friday 20 Nov at about 1,070 basis points, up roughly 139bp on the day and its highest in 13 months, local reports said on 21 Nov; that is above the 1,000bp mark widely read as distressed debt. A Criteria report cited on 21 Nov puts the shortfall against the government's 2027 financing plan at about US$7.75bn, as hard-dollar local debt auctions have been suspended for four straight rounds and the Treasury's expected year-end dollar cushion has shrunk. Weekend press in Buenos Aires carried speculation about whether Economy Minister Luis Caputo can withstand the pressure; nothing has been confirmed.
stories.market: The 2030 and 2035 sovereign notes fell more than 2 cents on the dollar on 20 Nov and dollar bonds are down about 20% since early August (Bloomberg); the wholesale peso closed at a record 1,580 per dollar on 20 Nov.

body: Argentina's sovereign spread over US Treasuries, as measured by JPMorgan's index, finished Friday 20 Nov at about 1,070 basis points after starting the session near 931, according to local market reports published on 21 Nov. The level is the highest in 13 months and compares with about 402bp on 10 July.

Bloomberg reported that Argentina led a broad emerging-market credit sell-off on Friday, with the 2030 and 2035 notes down more than 2 cents on the dollar by early afternoon in New York. Dollar bonds have lost about a fifth of their value since early August. The wholesale peso hit a nominal record of 1,580 per dollar, and the blue-chip swap rate stood at 1,744 on 19 Nov, an 11.4% gap over the official rate.

A report by Criteria, cited on 21 Nov, estimates a gap of about US$7.75bn against the official 2027 financing plan. About US$5bn reflects hard-dollar local debt sales that have been suspended for four consecutive auctions since 14 August, and about US$2.75bn reflects a smaller dollar cushion at end-2026: the plan assumed US$3.7bn, while the Treasury now holds roughly US$950m. Consultancy LCG estimates US$25.4bn of foreign-currency payments in 2027, including principal and interest on Bonares and Globales and payments to the IMF.

Analysts cite political risk ahead of the 2027 presidential election, slowing growth and monthly inflation that has not fallen below about 1.5%. Oppenheimer's Fernando Losada said election risk is elevated and will remain so, while VanEck's David Austerweil described Argentina as a crowded long without positive catalysts. LCG said it has no doubts about the government's willingness to pay.

stories.headline: Brazil's Lower House Schedules a Monday Vote on the Spending-Curb Bill
stories.summary: Chamber of Deputies president Hugo Motta has called an extraordinary session for Monday 23 Nov to vote on the government's fiscal-adjustment bill PLP 299/2026, reports dated 22 Nov said. Rapporteur Mauro Benevides kept the Senate text, which caps real spending growth at 2% in years when spending must be frozen, allows a 10% across-the-board cut in tax benefits and curbs tax-credit offsets, for an estimated impact of about R$50bn in 2027. An opposition amendment could still send the bill back to the Senate.
stories.market: The dollar closed at R$5.9350 on 19 Nov (+1.16%), up 4.87% on the week and at its highest since April 2025, despite a US$1bn central-bank sale; it was quoted near R$5.95 on 20 Nov while local markets were shut for a holiday.

body: Motta convened an extraordinary session of the Chamber for Monday 23 Nov to take up PLP 299/2026, the complementary bill the Senate finished approving on 18 Nov. Rapporteur Mauro Benevides (União-CE) kept the Senate's text, a choice aimed at sending the bill straight to the president.

The bill would limit real spending growth to 2% in years when the fiscal target is at risk, allow a 10% linear cut in tax benefits and sector subsidies, and let the government restrict cross-tax credit offsets. Companies used about R$200bn of such offsets in January-September 2026, according to Receita Federal data cited in the reports. The Senate rapporteur estimated the 2027 impact at about R$50bn, against an earlier R$45.1bn-56.1bn range.

Markets have been testing the package. The dollar rose for six straight sessions to close at R$5.9350 on 19 Nov, and the Ibovespa lost 3.53% on the week to 166,376. Some investors doubt the measures solve the structural rise in public debt, which the November Prisma Fiscal survey sees at 87.31% of GDP in 2027.

body: The naira lost ground every day of the week to 20 Nov at the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, with the biggest fall on 18 Nov, when it slid N16.99 to N1,379.99. Friday's range was N1,387.10 to N1,400.

Interbank turnover rose almost twelvefold over the week, from US$68.66m on Monday to US$815.57m on Friday, as the central bank supplied US$1.30bn. Nairametrics noted that turnover data do not show the direction of trades, so higher volume does not necessarily mean more dollar supply.

Cordros expects pressure to persist for the rest of 2026 but says reserve buffers are enough for continued intervention; Cowry Asset Management sees seasonal festive and import demand adding to strain. The MPC decision on 24 Nov will show whether the central bank leans on rates as well as reserves to steady the currency.

calendar.event: Taiwan's short-sale curbs on falling stocks take effect; first Asian session after the weekend Gulf strikes
calendar.why: Tests whether state support can steady the Taiex after its worst week since 1991.

calendar.event: Euro-zone flash PMIs for November (composite forecast 51.4)
calendar.why: First read on whether the sell-off and strikes are hitting European activity; a miss would add to bets against an ECB hike.

calendar.event: NATO allies discuss Russia's missile incursion into Poland in Brussels; Brazil's lower house votes on the spending-curb bill
calendar.why: Security risk for Polish assets; fiscal credibility for the real.

calendar.event: New York court hears the state's restraining-order request against Kalshi
calendar.why: Kalshi says the order could shut its exchange nationwide; read-through for DraftKings and Flutter.

calendar.event: Central Bank of Nigeria Monetary Policy Committee
calendar.why: The naira is near 1,400 per dollar despite heavy central-bank sales.

calendar.event: Earnings: Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Zoom, Agilent; $69bn US 2-year note auction earlier in the day
calendar.why: HPE's AI-server orders are a read-through for the hardware sell-off.

calendar.event: Earnings: Best Buy, Dollar Tree, Medtronic before the open; Dell, Workday, Autodesk, HP Inc. after the close. VW and IG Metall open pay talks in Emden
calendar.why: Dell's $95bn AI-server backlog is the week's key AI test.

calendar.event: US October PCE inflation, Q3 GDP, durable goods and jobless claims; Deere results before the open
calendar.why: Last PCE before the 9 December Fed decision, with a 25bp hike about 90% priced.

calendar.event: US markets closed for Thanksgiving; Crystal Crop Protection lists in India
calendar.why: Thin holiday liquidity can amplify moves after a volatile week.

calendar.event: Tokyo core CPI for November (forecast 3.0% vs 2.6%); US stocks close early (19:00 CET)
calendar.why: A jump would firm expectations of a Bank of Japan hike in December.
Polls point to a PP-Vox majority; matters for Spanish bonds and the IBEX 35.
